plain.text: In Caesarea lived Cornelius, a Roman centurion. He and his family were devout and God-fearing; he gave generously to the poor and prayed regularly. One afternoon he had a vision of an angel who said, "Your prayers and gifts to the poor have come up as a memorial before God. Send men to Joppa to bring back Simon who is called Peter." Cornelius sent two servants and a soldier.

About noon the next day, Peter went up on the roof to pray. He became hungry and fell into a trance. He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet let down, containing all kinds of animals, reptiles and birds. A voice said, "Get up, Peter. Kill and eat." "Surely not, Lord! I have never eaten anything impure or unclean." The voice said, "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean." This happened three times.

While Peter wondered about the vision, Cornelius's men arrived. The Spirit said, "Three men are looking for you. Go with them, for I have sent them." Peter invited them in as guests. The next day he set out with them.

Cornelius had gathered his relatives and close friends. When Peter came in, Cornelius fell at his feet. Peter made him get up: "Stand up, I am only a man myself." Peter said, "You know it is against our law for a Jew to visit a Gentile. But God has shown me that I should not call anyone impure or unclean." Cornelius explained his vision. "Now we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has commanded you to tell us."

Peter said, "I now realise how true it is that God does not show favouritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears him and does what is right." He told them about Jesus: anointed by God with the Holy Spirit and power, going around doing good and healing. They killed him by hanging him on a cross, but God raised him on the third day, and he appeared to witnesses who ate and drank with him. Jesus is the one God appointed as judge of the living and the dead. "All the prophets testify about him that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name."

While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message. The Jewish believers with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on Gentiles, for they heard them speaking in tongues and praising God. Peter said, "Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptised with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have." So he ordered them to be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ.

summary.bigIdea: God shows Peter that the good news is for every nation, and the Holy Spirit comes on Gentiles too.
points: Cornelius, a Roman soldier, seeks God and is told to send for Peter.
Peter's vision teaches him not to call anyone God has made clean "unclean".
"God does not show favoritism": the Spirit comes on Cornelius's household and they are baptised.
summary.reflection: Peter had to change his mind about who was welcome. Is there anyone you find it hard to see as welcome to God?
